findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the request cycle, so fallbacks silently fail elsewhere
findings.body: Locale files are loaded lazily: `I18n.translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)` for the *current* locale, and the new fallback locales are loaded exclusively by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any translation performed outside a web request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers that set `I18n.locale` per recipient, rake tasks, console, `I18n.t(key, locale: :xx)` calls) will therefore run with the fallback locales' translation data not loaded, so `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` finds nothing in the fallback chain and the user gets a "translation missing" string instead of the English/site-default text — exactly the case this feature is meant to fix. The loading of the fallback chain should happen inside `load_locale`/`translate` (or `ensure_loaded!` should be invoked from a single central place), not in a controller filter.

findings.title: Translation LRU cache key ignores the fallback chain, so results go stale when default_locale changes
findings.body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With the new fallbacks, the value returned for a given key/locale also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (the second entry of `FallbackLocaleList#[]`). When an admin changes the `default_locale` site setting, previously cached entries that were resolved through the old fallback locale remain in the LRU cache and keep being served for the lifetime of the process (nothing calls `I18n.reload!` on that setting change). Either include the resolved fallback chain in the cache key or clear `@cache` when `default_locale` changes.

findings.title: Fallback list is recomputed (with a SiteSetting read) on every lookup instead of being memoized
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList` subclasses `Hash` but overrides `#[]` to always recompute, so every call from `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` (which happens on *every* translation lookup, not just misses) performs a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read, a `to_sym`, and allocates two arrays (`uniq`, `compact`). Translation lookups with interpolation arguments bypass the LRU cache in translate_accelerator, so this runs on a hot path. Since the class is already a Hash, the computed chain should be memoized per locale and invalidated when `default_locale` changes.

findings.title: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` raises if the setting is nil, and `uniq` before `compact` cannot protect it
findings.body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on the setting value before any nil handling; if `SiteSetting.default_locale` is ever nil/blank (e.g. during early boot, or a site with a cleared setting) this raises `NoMethodError` from inside every translation lookup, which would surface as a 500 on all pages. The trailing `.compact` only removes nils that are already in the array (and `uniq` before `compact` is pointless), it does not guard the `to_sym` call. Use `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym` or a safe default.

findings.title: `@loaded_locales ||= []` in ensure_loaded! runs outside LOAD_MUTEX
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` lazily initializes `@loaded_locales` and tests `include?` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates the same ivar inside the mutex. If two threads hit `ensure_loaded!` while the ivar is still nil, both create their own array and one assignment is lost, so the record of already-loaded locales can be dropped and translation files are re-parsed (and the `include?` guard in `translate` can be defeated). Initialize `@loaded_locales` inside the mutex (or at load time) and perform the membership check under the same lock.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback behaviour
findings.body: The PR changes global I18n behaviour for all environments (fallbacks are now always enabled, with a custom chain user-locale → site default_locale → :en) and adds `I18n.ensure_loaded!`/`FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`, but no specs are added. There is no coverage asserting that a key missing in a user's locale resolves to the site default locale and then to English, that `default_locale` changes are honoured, or that the lazy locale loader loads every locale in the chain. Given the stale-cache and lazy-loading interactions involved, regressions here would be silent (users just see missing/English text). Note also that `FallbackLocaleList` is defined in an initializer, so it is neither autoloaded nor reloadable, which makes it hard to unit test.
